old_title: Michael Carrick LIVE: 'Deal done' to hire replacement ahead of crunch Man Utd summit
new_title: Carrick sacked LIVE: Pochettino lined up as Man Utd fire manager
old_text:

Michael Carrick's future as Manchester United manager is in severe doubt after overseeing the club's worst start to the Premier League season in 40 years and with his side in the relegation zone.
A second Old Trafford comeback of the week, this time battling from two goals down twice to rescue a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday, might not be enough to save Carrick's job and he is at risk of being sacked after just 10 games of the season and with his side 18th during the international break.
United ended a nine-game winless run when they came from two goals down to beat Roma in the Champions League last week but they have not won in eight attempts in the Premier League and have just one top-flight win this campaign.
Carrick survived crisis talks with the United hierarchy after defeats to Como and Bournemouth last month and was given time to turn results around, but speculation over a change begun the day after Sunday's chaotic draw and The Independent understands contact was made with United States boss Mauricio Pochettino over succeeding Carrick.
The Old Trafford hierarchy, including Jason Wilcox, Omar Berrarda and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, are set to meet in Monaco today to discuss Carrick's future as the club are reportedly close to agreeing a deal with Pochettino should they decide to move on from Carrick.
Follow latest updates from Old Trafford here:
Carrick back players despite struggles
There are many problems at Manchester United and one of the perceived issues, certainly with fans, is that the club have brought in players who are not good enough to excel at the club.
Diogo Dalot was the most recent recipent of the supporters' ire following the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa.
Dalot was substituted during the game and the decision to remove him was cheered.
"We've got to be careful with that, I think," Carrick said after the game.
"I understand the frustration. I understand the disappointment of the supporters, so I get it. We're all frustrated. We're all disappointed.
"The players are as much as anyone, I guarantee you that. Diogo gives absolutely everything. He's played in different positions. He's played left-back. He's played really well at times.
"He gives a penalty away. He knows that, maybe he can do a little bit better. Alright, that's part of it, he's made a mistake.
"But he cares an awful lot, and he's given everything, so I like what he brings to the team. I like what he brings to the group."
Carrick carrying on as normal
Michael Carrick spoke about Man Utd's tough run of results ahead of this current international break.
Following United's 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday, Carrick said: "Yeah, it's been a right mixed week or two or three, really, if you're looking at the events.
"But I'm pretty clear where we need to go and how we need to get there.
"Obviously some of the boys will be flying off around the world and different things, and the group will be split for 10 days or so.
"But as a normal international week is, you know, we'll have some training. We'll have one or two days off, but not too much. But we'll train, and we'll get ready for the next game."
BREAKING: Manchester United reach verbal agreement with Pochettino
Sky Sports News say that a verbal agreement in principle has been agreed betwen Mauricio Pochettino and Manchester United.
They say that United will want to move quickly if they sack Michael Carrick.
There are some details still to be worked out with Pochettino but the feelings are strong that no issues will occur.
United must talk to US Soccer to buy Pochettino out of his contract with the national team. That will also include a £7m fee + more if Pochettino's staff come with him.
Mauricio Pochettino becomes major candidate to replace Michael Carrick as Man United manager
The United States head coach has a contract until the 2030 World Cup but the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss could emerge as a candidate to succeed Michael Carrick with United lodged inside the relegation zone.
More candidates to possibly replace Michael Carrick
Antonio Conte
The appeal of the combustible Italian only has grown while United have been accused of becoming too passive and pedestrian on the pitch. Conte is one of the most demanding coaches in the game and would instantly bring a level of intensity and urgency that has been lacking this season, while his CV - with Serie A titles at Juventus, Inter Milan and Napoli and a Premier League crown with Chelsea - commands respect.
Conte also brought an immediate improvement when he took charge of a floundering Tottenham five years ago and led them back into the Champions League, which now has to be United's biggest concern. So the 57-year-old offers impact, but then what?
Conte has a sharp tongue and is not afraid to criticise his bosses if he feels they are failing to support him. His exit from Tottenham in March 2023 followed a stunning evisceration of the club in a now legendary press conference at Southampton.
United would be playing with fire but options of Conte's calibre are few and far between. Conte has also distanced himself from the Manchester United job while branding reports that he is in "advanced negotiations" with any club as "speculation".
More candidates to possibly replace Michael Carrick
Unai Emery
The Spaniard has done a superb job at Aston Villa by securing Champions League qualification and ending the club's trophy drought with victory in the Europa League.
But Aston Villa will be even more determined to keep Emery given the club are only in the early stages of their rebuild under him, having completely overhauled the spine of their team over the summer.
As it is, Emery enjoys complete control over his project at Villa Park, a reality he is unlikely to find at Old Trafford, while he appears enthused by the challenge of constructing a second competitive team in the Premier League.
With Emery, who is under contract until 2029, United would also need to pay Villa compensation, and that may place him above their budget.
Man Utd's upcoming fixtures
Should Carrick remain in charge or should he be replaced whoever is in the dugout following the international break will have a tricky start.
United's next fixture is against Liverpool in the Premier League before a run of games against clubs that could firmly place them in a relegation battle should they fail to win them.
These are United's next six fixtures:
Liverpool (A) - Premier League - Sunday November 22
Sporting (A) - Champions League - Wednesday November 25
Brentford (H) - Premier League - Saturday November 28
Newcastle (A) - Premier League - Wednesday December 2
Coventry (H) - Premier League - Saturday December 5
RB Leipzig (H) - Champions League - Tuesday December 8
Candidates to possibly replace Michael Carrick
Julian Nagelsmann
The former wunderkind of German coaching was reportedly on United's radar when they sacked Ruben Amorim at the start of the year, but as an option for the summer following the World Cup.
Well, that was a bit of a disaster for the former Bayern Munich and RB Leipzig coach, as Germany were knocked out in the last-32 by Paraguay.
Nagelsmann, 39, would naturally be interested in managing United and the club's director of recruitment, Christopher Vivell, previously worked with him at Red Bull.
Candidates to possibly replace Michael Carrick
Fabian Hurzeler
Brighton have been the surprise package in the Premier League this season and the 33-year-old Hurzeler has drawn praise for turning the Seagulls into a side capable of competing with the country's biggest clubs.
Brighton's 3-0 victory over champions Arsenal earlier this season was a masterclass in modern coaching while Hurzeler's side also knocked United out of the Carabao Cup with a brilliant 3-2 win at Old Trafford.
The Independent's Chief Football Writer Miguel Delaney has reported that Hurzeler is admired at Old Trafford but Brighton would demand significant compensation for the highly-rated German and United may not have the cash.
At Brighton, Hurzeler has also enjoyed an environment where the club have made all the right decisions off the pitch. At United, he would arguably be walking into the opposite.
Candidates to possibly replace Michael Carrick
Eddie Howe
Howe told the club he needed a break from management but the chance to take charge at Old Trafford, three months later, would surely be too good to turn down if an offer arrives.
The 48-year-old remains highly regarded in English football after taking over a Newcastle side in the relegation zone and leading them to the club's highest Premier League finish in two decades, as well as their first domestic silverware in 70 years.
Howe twice took Newcastle into the Champions League playing an energetic, high-intensity style of football that would be popular at Old Trafford.

Michael Carrick has been sacked as Manchester United manager after overseeing the club's worst start to the Premier League season in 40 years, with Mauricio Pochettino looking set to replace him.
A second Old Trafford comeback of the week, this time battling from two goals down twice to rescue a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday, was not enough to save Carrick's job and the club announced on Thursday that it had parted ways with him after just 10 games of the season and with his side 18th during the international break.
United ended a nine-game winless run when they came from two goals down to beat Roma in the Champions League last week but they have not won in eight attempts in the Premier League and have just one top-flight win this campaign.
Carrick survived crisis talks with the United hierarchy after defeats to Como and Bournemouth last month and was given time to turn results around, but speculation over a change begun the day after Sunday's chaotic draw and The Independent understands contact was initially made with United States boss Pochettino over succeeding Carrick on Monday.
The Old Trafford hierarchy, including Jason Wilcox, Omar Berrarda and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, met in Monaco to discuss Carrick's future and the club are on the verge of hashing out a deal with Pochettino, who is reportedly ready to accept the position.
Follow latest updates from Old Trafford here:
Are United 'late to the party' with Mauricio Pochettino?
Paul Scholes thinks Man United might be going in for Mauricio Pochettino a few years too late.
He said on The Good, The Bad & The Football: "I love Pochettino and we work with him at Soccer Aid, didn't we, he's a he's a great man. I think he's got the presence to manage a big football club like Manchester United.
"He's got the respect to do it. He works with young players which obviously Manchester United want. My only slight concern is have that we come a little bit too late to the party.
"I think we've done that in the past. You look at Van Gaal, his best years were probably behind him. Mourinho again, I think his best years were probably behind him. Saying that, I'm not ruling out what he's going to do with this Real Madrid team because this Real Madrid team look good.
"I just - when you really think about when we was talking about this two or three weeks ago after the Bournemouth game I don't think any of us mentioned Pochettino."
Man United Supporters' Trust underlines 'depressing moment' after Michael Carrick sacked
The Manchester United Supporters' Trust (MUST) has branded Michael Carrick's sacking "another depressing moment" and argued the club's problems rest primarily with its ownership, in a now-familiar plea to end the ongoing feeling of crisis at Old Trafford.
United sacked Carrick just 10 games into the Premier League season with the club in the relegation zone and having won just once in this domestic campaign.
The club's hierarchy met minority owner Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday to discuss Carrick's future and a statement on Thursday said that it had "come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions".
Bad day for managers
A particularly bleak stat from Opta.
Today is only the sixth time in Premier League history two managers - Michael Carrick and Pierre Sage - have left their positions on the same day during a season.
The last time it happened actually wasn't that long ago, with Wolves boss Gary O'Neil and Southampton manager Russell Martin both getting canned on 15 December 2024.
When will Mauricio Pochettino take charge of Manchester United?
Pochettino is still contracted to US Soccer until the 2030 World Cup though an early departure from his deal feels increasingly likely. United have made contact with US Soccer over paying compensation to release Pochettino with rumoured figures reaching as high a $10m (£7.4m).
Should an agreement be made, Pochettino could, in theory, leave the US before the scheduled games against Haiti in order to spend time with Man United's squad ahead of the crucial clash at Anfield.
In that case he could arrive at Carrington either the same day or a day after being formally announced as the new head coach. That would give him a maximum of nine days to prepare the team if his appointment is confirmed today (Thursday 12 November).
The more likelier option is that Pochettino leads the USMNT for their two fixtures with Haiti and reports to Carrington shortly afterwards.
In that case, he could be in post at Man United as early as Wednesday 18 November though given the time difference between the US and the UK, Pochettino would arrive late in the afternoon or early evening.
Even so, that would give him three full days, Thursday 19, Friday 20 and Saturday 21 to settle into his new environment and have time on the grass with the squad.
When will Mauricio Pochettino take charge of Manchester United?
Thoughts have now turned to Michael Carrick's replacement with former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain manager Mauricio Pochettino the odds on favourite to take over.
Pochettino is the current manager of the United States Men's National Team (USMNT) but has reportedly reached a verbal agreement with Man United to sign of as their new head coach. Should his appointment be confirmed when will Pochettino officially begin his tenure?
Man United's next match comes on Sunday 22 November when they travel to Anfield to take on Liverpool. It will arguably be the most difficult start possible for whoever takes over and it is a game United need to take something from or else they risk dropping further into the relegation zone.
The current international break would usually provide a new manager with time to train and see the squad in action but Pochettino, should he be given the job, is unlikely to have such a luxury.
That is because the United States have two Nations League matches to play on November 14 and 18 during this window and Pochettino is likely to oversee both fixtures.
Gary Neville hits out at 'classless' Man United
Gary Neville has branded Manchester United 'classless' over how they handled the dismissal of Michael Carrick.
United finally pulled the trigger on Carrick's sacking after days of leaving their manager in limbo, despite it becoming near-common knowledge that the club had been speaking to Mauricio Pochettino in an effort to acquire him as his replacement.
Speaking on the Overlap's Stick to Football podcast, which was recorded prior to Thursday's confirmation, he said: "We're sat here today recording this programme knowing that Michael Carrick is going to be sacked tomorrow, knowing that they're speaking to Mauricio Pochettino, knowing that they've spoken to (Julian) Nagelsmann, (Eddie) Howe - and they should be doing that by the way, I'm not saying they shouldn't be doing that...
"But I think the fact they're in Monaco now and they can't sack him today knowing that it's happening, to me it just feels a little bit clumsy, it feels a little bit classless.
"I think if you live in Monaco, you can't leave a guy hanging for 24 or 48 hours just because you live in Monaco, that can't happen."
Man United face final hurdle to close deal for Mauricio Pochettino as new manager
Manchester United are closing in on a deal to appoint Mauricio Pochettino before their next game against Liverpool following Michael Carrick's sacking.
United must strike a deal with US Soccer, with a solution required over the United States' next two international games in particular, while the club's hierarchy is meeting at a Monaco summit to finalise a decision over the club's manager.
Compensation, worth an initial $7m (£5.3m), will be a formality due to the clause in Pochettino's existing contract, that runs until the 2030 World Cup.
But one major hurdle remains to ensure Pochettino can arrive in time for the trip to Anfield.
Rio Ferdinand: 'Man United statement like ChatGPT'
Rio Ferdinand has shown his support for former Manchester United team-mate Michael Carrick after his sacking.
"Forever legend!" he posted on X. "Showed dignity and class as always."
He later criticised the club's official statement confirming his exit, posting: "Man United statement like ChatGPT... I wanna hear a voice!"
The Man United sack window
Manchester United's penchant for implosion during the first half of the season, often after a summer of intense financial backing, is quite evident from this stat.
The club's last five permanent managers have all been sacked between 28 October and 5 January.
It's almost as if recruitment and management are not aligned...
Pierre Sage sacked by Crystal Palace
When it rains, it pours.
Crystal Palace have sacked manager Pierre Sage after the club slumped to bottom of the Premier League table for the first time since December 2017.
The Frenchman moved to Selhurst Park on a three-year contract this summer after an impressive year at Lens, where he led the club to a runner-up finish in Ligue 1, won the Coupe de France and Trophee des Champions titles for the first time, and qualified for the Champions League.
But he was unable to replicate that success across his 16 games in all competitions at Palace, who have conceded the most goals of any top-flight side this season and claimed just seven points out of a possible 30 during his tenure, and sit two points off safety going into the November international break.
